tagline: A form, an embed widget, and a wall page

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-08-07; Starter $29/month monthly, about $24/month on yearly billing.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan holds 15 testimonials with unlimited widgets and walls.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 15 testimonials for the lifetime of the account, 1 collection form, 1 project, 1 seat and 5 sizzle credits/month; unlimited widgets and walls.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Unlimited testimonials, 3 forms, 1 project, 2 seats and 5 sizzle credits/month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited testimonials and forms, 5 projects, 5 seats and 5 sizzle credits/month.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 15 testimonials total for the lifetime of the account, 1 form, 1 project, 1 seat and 5 sizzle credits/month; unlimited widgets and walls.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); no traditional trial because the Free plan is permanent
pricing.hiddenCosts: The 15-testimonial free cap never resets, and deleting testimonials does not restore capacity; later submissions are collected but hidden. Pro charges $10/month per extra project and $5/month per extra seat.

verdictSummary: A form, an embed widget, and a wall page. $300/yr for what is essentially a guestbook.
name: Senja / Testimonial.to
notes: A form, an embed widget, and a wall page. $300/yr for what is essentially a guestbook.
whatYouLose: a hosted collection URL that isn't yours

alternatives.name: Real Testimonials
alternatives.desc: Another WordPress route: forms, moderation, grids and sliders are free; video and the clever automation live upstairs.

facts.install: Install and activate the plugin from WordPress Plugins → Add New
facts.dataFormat: Testimonials, form submissions and display settings live in the site's WordPress database; reviewer images and other uploaded media live in the WordPress media library
facts.gapVsPaid: It is WordPress-only and less convenient than Senja/Testimonial.to for sending a hosted collection link, accepting video, importing proof and embedding polished widgets on any site.
facts.setupBlocker: It only works inside a self-hosted WordPress site, so a non-WordPress site first needs an entire WordPress installation

alternatives.name: Shosay
alternatives.desc: Unlimited text, video and audio proof, imports, walls and 25-plus widgets; the bill is zero, the tiny Powered by pill is not.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then paste an iframe/widget embed into the site
facts.dataFormat: Testimonials and account data live in Shosay's hosted PostgreSQL service, while uploaded images/media use Cloudflare R2; users can export their testimonials
facts.gapVsPaid: The free service is unusually complete, but every widget keeps a Powered by Shosay pill and its automation, integrations and branding controls are less mature.
facts.setupBlocker: You need permission to paste Shosay's embed code into the site, and every free widget carries a small Powered by Shosay pill

alternatives.name: Strong Testimonials
alternatives.desc: A WordPress-only form, moderation queue, grid, slider and widget; simple enough once you already own the WordPress problem.

facts.install: Install and activate from WordPress Plugins → Add New
facts.dataFormat: Testimonials and front-end form submissions live in the site's WordPress database; images use the site's WordPress media storage, and optional notification emails can contain submitted fields
facts.gapVsPaid: It needs WordPress and offers a more manual form-and-shortcode workflow, without the paid services' universal hosted page, easy video collection, imports and cross-platform widgets.
facts.setupBlocker: It requires a self-hosted WordPress site; the free edition has one collection form and lacks built-in captcha, so public forms may need another anti-spam layer

rejectedAlternatives.name: Famewall
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan stops at 10 testimonials and one video; useful demo, not a permanent replacement.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Reviewskits
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A young headless stack with 52 stars, no releases, and an SDK-shaped hole where the no-code widget should be.

prompt:
Build me a testimonial collection and display tool like Senja. Requirements:

- A public /submit page: name, role/company, avatar upload (or auto-fetch from a
  provided URL), star rating, and the testimonial text. Store submissions in SQLite
  with an approved flag defaulting to false.
- An /admin page (basic-auth from .env) listing submissions with approve/delete
  buttons · nothing shows publicly until approved.
- A public /wall page: masonry grid of approved testimonials, clean cards with
  avatar, name, stars, and text. Mobile-friendly, dark mode support.
- An embeddable widget: /embed.js renders the wall into any page via one script
  tag + a div, iframe-free, styled to inherit the host page's font.
- Image uploads resized server-side to 128px avatars, stored on disk.
- Node or Python, single small server, deploy instructions for a VPS.
